text: Their Pluto sits on the part of you that says yes. Jupiter is your appetite for scale: what you take to be possible, what you are willing to promise, how large a plan gets before you start checking it. Joined to their depth, that appetite stops being casual. An idea you would normally float and forget acquires a floor under it and a date attached. Near them you make bigger claims than usual, and you mean them more. What comes from their end is weight. They do not leave things small, so whatever you enlarge gets carried out to its real consequences. You name a direction and they want to know who pays for it, who it costs, what it looks like in the third year. That can be the most useful attention your optimism has ever had. It can also feel like being audited for enthusiasm, since most people let your large statements go by and they do not. What you supply is permission, and at this end of their chart permission is not a small thing to receive. Intensity of their kind often runs underground, rationed rather than spent, held back by an old sense that wanting on that scale is not allowed. Your belief says otherwise, mostly by example rather than by argument. In your company what they had been keeping in reserve starts to look like a program instead of a private appetite. That transfer does not run backward easily once it has happened. Together the two of you tend toward ambition of a size that surprises onlookers. Money, access, a cause, an institution, a body of work: whatever the shared subject is, this pairing takes it seriously and takes it far. You are the reason the aim is big. They are the reason it has teeth. In practical terms, plans made with this person do not stay in the talking stage, and other people start treating the two of you as one position rather than two. What gets exposed is what your generosity is for. Under this much pressure the difference between giving and buying becomes visible, first in small things: the favor with a shape to it, the encouragement that expects a particular answer. Their end reads that quickly, though they may say nothing about it for a long time. On your side you can find yourself certain about something you have not examined, because certainty is easier to hold when a person of that conviction is standing next to you. A conjunction leaves you no distance from which to check. The overreach is worth naming plainly. Nothing inside this contact says stop. Scale on top of depth is how a reasonable plan becomes a crusade, and how a fair opinion hardens into doctrine that admits no version of the other side. Neither of you supplies the brake, so it has to come from outside or from a habit of asking that you keep on purpose. You grow here by learning what your faith actually costs to hold. Belief that has been through scrutiny of this kind is a different instrument from the belief you started with: slower, more expensive, and much harder to knock over.

This one can sit unused for years and nothing will go wrong. Your Jupiter and their Pluto reach each other at a workable angle, so your sense of scale and their sense of depth are available to one another whenever either of you decides to pick the connection up. Nothing about the geometry does the picking up for you. Worth knowing early, because this contact never announces itself the way the harder angles do. Taken up, it works like this. You open the frame first, because that is what you do with anything: how far this could go, who else it touches, which of the limits everybody accepts are load-bearing. They come back with where the leverage actually sits. Not the polite answer about the plan, the real one about who controls the piece that matters. A single question from them can spare you a season of effort spread thin across the wrong ground. You rarely take that as being cut down, which is this angle's particular mercy. It lands as information rather than judgment, and your optimism survives it better aimed than before. Range is what you put in. They tend to work in a narrow beam, very deep and not very wide, and a beam like that finds it hard to imagine the same force spent on something larger or further off or less personal. You keep proposing the wider frame. Near you they take on things they would have called grandiose in anyone else's mouth, with their usual thoroughness still attached. In shared work the combination suits anything needing both nerve and reach: a long campaign, a negotiation with real money in it, an undertaking most people would consider too big to begin. You raise the ambition and they secure the base, and neither of you has to argue the other into position, which is unusual for these two bodies in any chart. One more use, less obvious than the others. This person can hear your honest opinion about money, influence, and what you would do with more of either, without flinching and without turning it into a moral question. The reverse holds. Conversations of that kind are rare, and they tend to change what you think you are permitted to want. Left alone, the whole thing stays pleasant and unremarkable. You will feel now and then that the two of you could do something serious together, then the week will offer something lighter, and nothing anywhere will object. No pressure attaches to this angle, which is exactly why nothing here gets built by accident. What builds it is the deliberate ask: bring them the thing you actually intend rather than the one you have already handled, and let their read stand when it contradicts yours. A few rounds of that and your plans start surviving contact with the world, which your Jupiter does not manage unassisted. The offer keeps standing either way, and that is precisely what makes it so easy to walk past.

Your Jupiter wants the door left open. Their Pluto wants to know who holds the key, what is behind it, and what it would take to keep it. Those two positions grind on each other here, and not occasionally. The grinding shows in how a plan gets discussed, in what counts as a fair offer, in the gap between believing a thing is possible and knowing exactly what it would cost. You are likely to feel it first as a chill on your enthusiasm. Say what you think could happen and the response is not the agreeable noise you are used to. It is a pause, then a question about the part of it you skipped, then a silence you cannot read. Some of those silences are judgments. Most are only depth of that kind taking its time to surface an answer. Whichever it is, you have stopped, and stopping is the one thing your function has never learned to do well. From their side, your ease is the provocation. You extend faith casually, offer room you have not measured, and treat large questions as open when they experience those questions as long settled and expensive. What you call generous can land as careless with something they have carried at cost. Their replies may come back heavier than the subject appeared to justify, and the extra weight is rarely about the subject. Underneath the arguments is a question about permission, and it belongs to both of you. You believe things ought to be allowed. They know that allowing is a decision somebody makes, and they pay close attention to who gets to make it. That is why disputes between you slide so fast from the surface topic to the terms: not what the plan is, but whose plan it is, and what the yes was in exchange for. The exposure runs your way more than you would choose. Hard angles make motives show, and pressure of this kind tends to surface whatever your optimism was sparing you from looking at. The permission you extend can turn out to carry a price you never stated, including to yourself. The belief you defend hardest may be the one that costs you least to hold. None of that is a charge against you. It is what this angle does to anybody standing in it. What it produces in exchange arrives as anything but comfort. Faith pushed on by someone who will not accept the pleasant version comes out sturdier and far better informed. Your sense of what is possible may narrow and get much more accurate at the same time, and you may find you can state what you want without dressing it up as a favor to everyone. The failure mode is the standoff: you keep expanding, they keep concentrating, and each of you treats the other as proof of the position you already held. That loop runs for years under a civil surface, and it is recognizable by the same disagreement showing up under a fresh heading. What changes things is naming the want as a want, with no larger justification wrapped around it. Put that way it can be argued about, and an argument you can actually have is worth more to both of you than a truce.

Scale and depth move between you without resistance, which is pleasant and slightly hazardous. Your Jupiter finds their Pluto with no effort at all. What you hold to be possible, they are prepared to make actual, and the handover happens before either of you has argued for it. Most people meet a large ambition with some form of caution. This person does not. The first thing you notice is that they take your reach seriously. Not politely: seriously, in the sense of asking what it would require and then holding on to the answer. Your habit is to open the frame. Their habit is to find the point of maximum leverage inside whatever frame is open. The two habits fit so neatly that plans between you often skip the stage where somebody talks you out of it. What flows the other way is a kind of nerve you may be short of. Belief is the part you are good at; staying is not. They will stay with a difficult thing long past the point where interest runs out, keep pressure on when nothing visible is happening, and be unpopular for as long as it takes. Around them your large intentions pick up a follow-through you cannot always produce on your own. Your contribution counts for as much. Intensity with no wide subject turns on itself, and this contact keeps handing theirs a horizon: a cause worth that much force, a body of work, a reason to spend it on something outside their own history. You may never see how much that alters for them, since the alteration is quiet and they do not tend to report it. In practice the pair tends to be effective around resources and standing. Money, access, reputation, whatever the shared field trades in, the two of you move it well and feel comfortable doing so. That comfort is the risk. Ease removes the moment where somebody asks whether this is still a good idea. Smooth angles include no point of resistance, so escalation feels like the next reasonable step, and together you can go considerably further than either of you would alone without ever noticing a line go by. There is a milder failure, which is that none of it gets used. Nothing here demands anything. You can enjoy this person's company for a decade, feel the fit, put nothing through it, and the ease will go on pretending the connection is being spent. The other thing to watch is where the hard edge comes from. You can end up outsourcing it to them, keeping your own hands clean while enjoying what the edge brings in, and then supplying the reasons that make the whole arrangement sound generous. Over years this contact offers something uncommon. Someone who meets your ambition at its actual size, does not call it too much, and is still working on it after the excitement has gone is not a person you run into often. What it asks in exchange is that you keep your own judgment awake, since nothing in the geometry will do that job on your behalf.

Across from everything you are prepared to believe sits everything they decline to take on faith. That is the axis. Your Jupiter looks at a situation and sees where it could go. Their Pluto looks at the same situation and sees what is buried in it, who is exposed, and what will not survive contact. Neither view is wrong, and neither one dissolves into the other, so both stay in the room. You are likely to experience this as being met by a person who cannot be talked up. Encouragement, which usually works for you, does not work here. Where most people accept the wider picture and feel better, they start looking for what the wider picture is covering. Your instinct to open things out reaches them as a move on something they are guarding, whether or not you intended anything of the sort. The reply comes back with a lot behind it, and frequently after a delay. The pressure you put on them is different in kind. They tend to treat certain subjects as settled long ago, at a price. You keep suggesting that the settlement could be reopened, that more is available, that the ceiling they describe is a wall somebody built. From your chair that is hope. From theirs it can look like a stranger wandering around a room they paid for. Power is the recurring subject even when neither of you uses the word. An opposition organizes around one axis, and here the axis is usually who decides: which of you sets the terms, who is being generous to whom, whether an offer was a gift or a claim. In shared enterprise it surfaces as disagreements about size and control that are never quite about the number under discussion. In closer bonds it becomes a long negotiation over what each of you is allowed to want out loud. There is a trade of disowned material running underneath, and it goes both ways. You can assign all the ambition to their side and stand back as the reasonable one who merely believes in things. They can assign all the naivety to yours and leave unexamined the part of themselves that would like to be talked into something. While that trade is running, each of you is arguing with your own material, and the actual disagreement waits. The completing half is what an opposition is for. Your reach is genuine and comes with no instinct for cost. Their depth is genuine and comes with no instinct for daylight. Facing that in someone you cannot dismiss teaches you what a plan weighs, in a way no agreeable friend could manage, and it gives them the news that opening something up is not the same as losing it. The two views are not going to reconcile. They are opposite by construction, and the pull between them is the usable part: it keeps your optimism from floating off and keeps their intensity from sealing over. What tends to stay with you, whatever the connection turns into, is a sharper figure for what your beliefs cost to act on. That number is hard to arrive at alone, and this is the sort of company in which it gets worked out.
